Subject: Post-demo: Dedicated perf validation & sizing proposal

Sarah — great meeting earlier, thanks for walking us through the Acme inference patterns. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the Dedicated capacity validation we discussed: 

Summary of Acme targets we captured on the call:
- Latency SLO: P95 latency <= 200 ms for streaming responses (token-by-token) and end-to-end request completion target ~< 600 ms for 1024-token responses.
- Throughput: 150 sustained requests/sec during peak window (business hours), spiky bursts to 400 rps for short periods.
- Concurrency: up to 60 concurrent active sessions with streaming enabled.
- Context: median prompt length ~120 tokens, max 4k tokens in test set.

Recommended validation plan (attached): redwood_perf_validation_plan.pdf — Marissa will lead a short perf sweep comparing H100 and A100 profiles and produce a sizing recommendation for Reserved Capacity (baseline and buffer). High-level ask from Redwood: provide a 1-hour validation window and a 2–3 representative prompt set (or a Drive folder link).

Immediate next steps:
1) Confirm the SLO numbers above (please reply with any edits).
2) Share sample prompts / dataset link and a rough expected QPS distribution.
3) Approve our proposed validation window (we recommend Thu 03/05 09:00–13:00 PT).
4) We will run head-to-head tests and deliver: measured P50/P95/P99 latencies, token throughput, and recommended reserved capacity (GPU type + quantity), plus a cost estimate and SLA draft.

Attachments: redwood_perf_validation_plan.pdf, SLA-draft-Redwood-vs-Acme.docx

Thanks — I’ll coordinate logistics once we have confirmation.

Thanks Karthik — that aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications before we lock the window: 

1) Streaming latency: when you say P95 <= 200 ms, is that per-token latency (token arrival cadence) or end-to-end for short responses? We really care about per-token cadence for our user experience.
2) Concurrency: the 60 concurrent sessions number is a firm limit for our initial rollout. During stress tests we might want to validate up to 120 to see safety margins.
3) Cost: can you give a rough order-of-magnitude cost delta between 8x H100 reserved vs 16x A100 (same generation) for a monthly reserved commitment? A ballpark range is fine for procurement to start the internal discussion.

We can share a Drive folder with 200 sample prompts (varied lengths). Thu 03/05 09:00–13:00 PT works for our engineering lead to be on the call. Please include Marissa for tech coordination.

—Sarah

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Dedicated perf validation & sizing proposal

Hi Sarah — quick technical notes ahead of the Thursday run so we’re aligned on expectations and measurements.

On latency semantics:
- We’ll report both per-token emit latency (measured at token-level for streaming) and end-to-end request latency (time to last token).
- Target P95 <= 200 ms per-token is achievable on H100 configs for models in the 7–20B range with appropriate batching disabled for low latency; on A100 you can hit similar per-token cadence but may need higher instance counts depending on model variant and quantization.

Sizing roughs (ballpark, to be validated by Thursday sweep):
- H100 baseline: 8x H100 (reserved) — expected sustained throughput ~200–250 generated tokens/sec per GPU depending on model; with 8 GPUs we expect to comfortably handle 150 requests/sec at your median prompt sizes with headroom for bursts.
- A100 baseline: 16x A100 — roughly similar aggregate throughput but higher footprint. Operationally H100 gives better single-stream latency and fewer nodes to manage.

Concurrency & burst handling:
- We’ll run tests at concurrent session counts: 60 (target), 90 (buffer), 120 (stress). We’ll also validate short burst scenarios to 400 rps.

Test harness & metrics we’ll publish:
- P50/P90/P95/P99 token and request latencies, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates for repeated prefixes, and per-route cost estimate.

Prep asks from Acme engineering:
- Drive folder with 200 prompts and an expected distribution file (we can ingest a simple CSV).
- Indicate which model variants you want us to test (open model names or LLM family). If you don’t specify, we’ll test the top 2 recommended by Redwood for your workload.

I attached the detailed perf plan (redwood_perf_validation_plan.pdf) which includes the exact harness commands, expected data outputs, and the verification checklist for the SLA draft. For cost delta, I’ll include a high-level table in the Thursday deliverable — but initial estimate: 8x H100 reserved typically lands ~15–30% premium vs 16x A100 on hardware cost but lower operational overhead and better latency profile. Exact numbers will depend on term length and committed v. burst capacity.

If everyone is good, I’ll provision the cluster in our staging Dedicated fleet on Thu morning and share access details.

—Marissa
